items.summary: Input/Output types on every function at every layer
items.details: Non-negotiable. Every orchestrator method, every repository method, every service method has *Input and *Output types. Never accept positional args. Never return bare types. Even helpers should use this pattern. This enables adding fields without breaking callers and future pagination.

items.summary: No proto types past the handler boundary
items.details: Handlers import and use pb. types for conversion. Orchestrators speak internal entity types ONLY. No pb. imports in orchestrators, services, repositories, or entity files. If a type needs to flow past the handler, define a local entity struct for it. The encounter orchestrator currently violates this — 39 pb. refs in orchestrator.go and 3 in service.go. These are tracked violations, not approved patterns.

items.summary: Test suites with gomock at interface boundaries
items.details: Use testify/suite for all test organization. Use go.uber.org/mock (gomock) for mocking at interface boundaries — not mockery. Place mocks in mock/ subdirectory next to the interface, using package name <domain>mock. Regenerate with go:generate.

items.summary: Constructor validates config at startup
items.details: Every New() or NewX() constructor validates its Config struct. If a required dependency is nil, return an error immediately. Never nil-check at runtime in methods. Fail fast at startup.

items.summary: Never return (nil, nil)
items.details: Every function returns either a valid non-nil output or an error. Empty results use empty structs or empty slices, not nil. This applies at every layer.

items.summary: Auth context extraction at handler, passed explicitly to orchestrator
items.details: Handlers call auth.PlayerIDFromContext(ctx) and pass playerID as a field in the orchestrator's input struct. The orchestrator does not access the context for auth. This keeps auth logic in one layer.

items.summary: Outside-in development: handler stub → interface → tests → implementation → repository
items.details: Start with a gRPC handler returning codes.Unimplemented. Define the service interface and Input/Output types. Write handler tests with mocked service. Implement the orchestrator. Implement the repository last. See docs/how-to/add-handler-method.md.

items.summary: Load-then-stream pattern for real-time encounter state
items.details: Clients call GetEncounterState to get a full snapshot with LastEventID, then call StreamEncounterEvents with last_event_id to receive only new events. The orchestrator updates LastEventID in EncounterData whenever an event is published. This is the canonical multi-player state sync pattern.

items.summary: Game logic belongs in rpg-toolkit, not rpg-api
items.details: If code checks weapon properties, calculates modifiers, evaluates conditions, or implements D&D rules — it belongs in rpg-toolkit. rpg-api passes entities to toolkit functions and persists results. The dungeon component is currently violating this boundary and is scheduled for migration.

items.summary: make pre-commit before every commit; make ci-check before every push
items.details: pre-commit runs: fmt, tidy, fix-eof, lint, test. ci-check runs scripts/ci-checks.sh for CI-specific validations. Never use --no-verify. If pre-commit fails, fix the issue — CI will fail with the same checks.

items.summary: Apply room origin at the merge boundary; cumulative encounter state is dungeon-absolute
items.details:
When folding revealed-room data (walls, entities, obstacles, monster placements) into cumulative encounter state, translate from room-local to dungeon-absolute at the producer using dungeon.Module.LocalToAbsolute (or the localToAbsoluteOrLocal helper in orchestrator.go for the single-room start case). Do this at the OpenDoor merge site, not at downstream consumers.

Producers that write to cumulative state and must apply origin:
- buildRoomLayoutProto (orchestrator.go ~1098): walls in EncounterStateData.rooms[].walls.
- localToAbsoluteOrLocal at OpenDoor (~3172): monster.Position in MonsterInfo / Entities map.
- buildCombinedRoomDataAfterOpenDoor (~5836): obstacle.Position in spatial.RoomData.CubeEntities.

Consumers (handlers, event publishers, perception, movement-collision, roomContainingPosition) treat cumulative state as already-absolute and never re-translate. The proto RoomLayout.Origin field is still emitted alongside absolute walls so a client can recover the local frame by subtraction if needed.

If you add a new producer of cumulative state and skip origin translation, you reproduce issue #493. Enforce this at code review for any new merge site.

items.summary: v1alpha2 encounter has no orchestrator layer — handler talks directly to the toolkit Encounter + Broker
items.details:
Architecture Honesty (chapter 1) move shipped in PR #496. Where v1alpha1 has handler → orchestrator → engine, v1alpha2 has handler → toolkit-encounter-SDK directly. The Boundary Rule still holds: game rules live in rpg-toolkit/encounter (Move, Snapshot, PerceptionView). rpg-api becomes a thinner shim — load Data, call verb, save Data, translate events.

When adding a v2 RPC: do NOT introduce an orchestrator. Add a method on the Handler in internal/handlers/dnd5e/v2/encounter/handler.go (or a new file in that package). The handler holds *encounter.Broker, encountersv2.Repository, and a now func() time.Time injected via HandlerConfig.

If you find yourself wanting an orchestrator ("too much logic in the handler"), the right move is usually to push the logic into rpg-toolkit/encounter, not to add an orchestrator layer. File a toolkit issue for the missing helper.

items.summary: v1alpha2 encounter file layout established by slice 1
items.details:
PR #496 established this layout. New v2 work fits this shape — don't reinvent it.

Handler (one package per service):
  internal/handlers/dnd5e/v2/encounter/
    handler.go        — Handler struct, New(*HandlerConfig), MoveEntity, StreamEncounter
    handler_test.go   — handler unit tests with mocked Broker/Repo
    translate.go      — toolkit-event → proto-envelope translator + ErrViewerSawNothing/ErrUnknownEventType
    translate_test.go — translator unit tests per event type

Repository (in-memory + Redis, both implement encountersv2.Repository):
  internal/repositories/encounters/v2/
    repository.go  — Repository interface (Get, Save, ErrNotFound, etc.)
    in_memory.go   — NewInMemory() — round-trips through ToData/LoadFromData
    redis.go       — Redis-backed; encoding via toolkit serializer
    *_test.go      — both implementations covered by the same suite

Integration tests (bufconn — slice 1 gate test):
  internal/integration/encounter_v2_test.go — EncounterV2IntegrationSuite
  internal/integration/harness/harness.go    — extension fields TestServer.{EncounterClientV2, BrokerV2, EncRepoV2}; harness.New seeds + registers v2 service alongside v1alpha1

Server wiring:
  cmd/server/server.go — registers v2 service alongside v1alpha1; both alive.

items.summary: v2 Broker is process-scoped on the server struct, in-memory transport for now
items.details:
The encounter Broker (rpg-toolkit/encounter.Broker) is constructed once at server startup over tkenc.NewInMemoryTransport() and held on the server struct. The same Broker instance is shared between the handler that publishes (Move, future OpenDoor/Attack) and StreamEncounter that subscribes. There is one Broker per process — encounters are keyed by EncounterID inside the Broker, not via separate Broker instances.

Do not construct a per-request Broker. Do not pass Brokers through the request path. Inject the process-scoped Broker into HandlerConfig at startup.

Future: Redis transport when we go multi-process. The interface is pluggable but slice 1 doesn't ship it. See rpg-toolkit/encounter docs for transport contract.

items.summary: v2 translator uses ErrViewerSawNothing / ErrUnknownEventType sentinels; stream loop is errors.Is-aware
items.details:
translate.go's TranslateEvent(evt, viewer, now) returns three error shapes the stream loop must handle distinctly:

  - ErrViewerSawNothing: the broker delivered an event to this viewer but the viewer's per-player slice is empty (e.g. MoveEvent's PerPlayer[viewer].SeenSegments is empty). The stream loop SILENTLY continues — do not log, do not send.
  - ErrUnknownEventType: the translator has no mapping for the concrete event type (a new toolkit event landed that the translator doesn't know yet). The stream loop LOGS via log.Printf with encounter+type, then continues. This surfaces the gap in production.
  - any other error: a real bug. Stream loop returns codes.Internal.

When adding a new toolkit event to the translator: add a case in the TranslateEvent type-switch, write a translate<EventType> helper that handles per-viewer slicing, and add a translate_test.go case. Do NOT swallow ErrViewerSawNothing in the helper — return it to the loop.

items.summary: v2 integration tests use the bufconn harness; encounter is constructed via tkenc.New + harness.EncRepoV2.Save
Toolkit Move errors → FailedPrecondition; empty proposed_path → InvalidArgument
items.details:
Settled mid-flight in slice 1 (rpg-api#495 closed by PR #496). Toolkit encounter.Move returns errors for state-dependent failures: turn order mismatch, blocked path, out-of-range, entity-not-in-encounter. These are gRPC FailedPrecondition by convention — the request was syntactically valid but the world state forbids the action.

The one truly argument-shaped error is empty proposed_path — caught BEFORE Move is called and returned as InvalidArgument.

Apply the same convention to future v2 verbs: state-dependent → FailedPrecondition; truly malformed input → InvalidArgument; auth → PermissionDenied; missing entity/encounter → NotFound; auth missing → Unauthenticated.

Document any new mapping in rpg-api/docs/architecture/components/encounter.md.

items.summary: ProjectFor is the single source of truth for converting (encounter.Data, viewer) → proto Encounter; never inline projection
items.details:
Validated in Wave 2.6 (PR #501 extracted, #502 broadened, #503 reused). Located at `internal/handlers/dnd5e/v2/encounter/project.go`. Signature:

  func ProjectFor(data *encounter.Data, viewer core.PlayerID, broker *encounter.Broker, now time.Time) (*encounterv2pb.Encounter, error)

Responsibilities:
- Calls `encounter.LoadFromData(data, broker)` and `enc.SnapshotFor(viewer)` to get the toolkit Snapshot.
- Iterates `data.Players` (sorted by player ID for determinism) and includes the viewer plus any non-viewer player whose `View.Position` is within the viewer's current sight range via `perception.VisibleHexesAt(snap.Position, sightRange)`.
- Translates revealed hexes from the viewer's `View.RevealedHexes` to the proto wire shape.

Used by: CreateEncounter handler (returns the projection in CreateEncounterResponse.encounter), GetEncounter handler (same), StreamEncounter snapshot replay (feeds both TranslateSnapshot and BuildReplayEvents — see pat-v2-snapshot-replay-builder-pair).

When adding a new RPC or stream-side flow that needs a per-viewer snapshot of an encounter, call ProjectFor. Do NOT inline the projection logic. If ProjectFor needs broadening for a future shape (entities beyond players, condition visibility, last-known-position for ghosts), extend ProjectFor — keep the single seam.

items.summary: StreamEncounter on connect emits SnapshotDelivered + synthetic replay events; TranslateSnapshot + BuildReplayEvents share the ProjectFor output
items.details:
Pattern shipped in PR #503 (#497). The StreamEncounter handler's connect sequence:

  1. Subscribe(encID, viewer) — buffered channel begins capturing live events
  2. encRepo.Get + LoadFromData — load + rehydrate
  3. enc.SnapshotFor(viewer) — toolkit snapshot
  4. ProjectFor(data, viewer, broker, now) — build proto Encounter ONCE
  5. TranslateSnapshot(snap, projected, now) — wraps as SnapshotDelivered envelope
  6. BuildReplayEvents(projected, snap, now) — synthesizes []EntityAppeared + GeometryRevealed
  7. stream.Send(SnapshotDelivered) + each replay event
  8. live forward loop drains buffered channel

Key design decisions:
- ProjectFor runs ONCE; both TranslateSnapshot and BuildReplayEvents consume its `*pbEncounter` output. Neither duplicates projection logic.
- TranslateSnapshot signature now takes `*pbEncounter` (was untyped before #503's drive-by) so it doesn't need to know about projection.
- Both helpers exported (capitalized) so external `_test` package can exercise them directly.
- Subscribe-before-snapshot ordering preserved: live events that fire during steps 2-7 are buffered and delivered after the replay completes. Tests cover this with `TestStreamEncounter_LiveEventsDoNotDuplicateReplay`.
- 'initial state' string is the Reason on synthetic replay events (file `BuildReplayEvents`); could become a constant if more reason strings accumulate. Two PR reviewers flagged it as deferred-cleanup — file an issue if a third reviewer mentions it.

When adding new event types to v2 that need to be present in the initial scene a viewer connects to: extend BuildReplayEvents to synthesize the corresponding initial-state shape from ProjectFor's output.

items.summary: Interact RPC dispatches to a toolkit verb by target-type discriminator (door/chest/lever/...)
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.7 (rpg-api PR #506). The Interact handler is a thin dispatch:

  1. Auth: pull viewer PlayerID from ctx.
  2. Load: encRepo.Get(req.encounter_id) + encounter.LoadFromData(data, broker).
  3. Validate target.case oneof — currently only `door` is implemented; new target types add a case here.
  4. Dispatch: switch on target.case → call the matching toolkit verb on the encounter aggregate (door → enc.OpenDoor(viewer, doorRef)). The handler does not implement the verb; rules live in rpg-toolkit/encounter.
  5. Save: encRepo.Save(enc.ToData()).
  6. Live events flow via the broker on their own — handler does NOT manually publish the outcome events.

When adding a new target type to Interact (chest, lever, trap, NPC dialogue start):
  - Add the toolkit verb on rpg-toolkit/encounter first; let it emit its own cause + effect events.
  - Add the case in the handler's target-type switch; map proto target ref to toolkit input.
  - Map toolkit errors via pat-v2-status-code-mapping (state-dependent → FailedPrecondition; missing target → NotFound).
  - Extend the translator (translate.go) for any new event types the verb publishes.

Do NOT inline the verb's logic in the handler — that's the same orchestrator anti-pattern pat-v2-handler-direct-no-orchestrator warns against, just renamed.

items.summary: Translator must NOT combine cause + effect events; toolkit deliberately decouples them and the wire keeps them separate
items.details:
Validated across Waves 2.7 (DoorOpened/HexRevealed) and 2.8 (AttackResolved/DamageDealt/ConditionApplied). The toolkit publishes cause-stage events (DoorOpenedEvent, AttackResolvedEvent) AND effect-stage events (HexRevealedEvent, DamageDealtEvent, ConditionAppliedEvent) as separate events with separate per-viewer projections. The rpg-api translator MUST NOT collapse a cause + effect into a single wire message.

Rationale (from Wave 2.7 design + verified 2.8):
  - Different viewers may see only one half. Player A sees the door open from inside the room (cause); player B sees the new hexes reveal but didn't perceive the cause (e.g. stealth scenario).
  - Different consumers care about different halves. Animations hook the cause ("play attack swing"), HP UI hooks the effect ("-5 HP").
  - The narrative log uses both as distinct lines ("goblin attacks alice" vs "alice takes 5 damage").

Translator rule: one toolkit event → at most one proto wire event. If the toolkit publishes 3 events for a single verb, the wire emits 3 events. Per-viewer slicing happens independently for each.

Validated reality note (2026-05-09): AttackResolvedEvent does NOT reach the wire today. dnd5e action layer uses a stand-in resolver in the encounter SDK instead of routing through combat.ResolveAttack — only DamageDealtEvent + ConditionAppliedEvent fire on the wire for the goblin's attack. Tracked as rpg-toolkit#635. Once #635 lands, the cause-stage AttackResolved will start flowing and the translator's existing AttackResolved case will activate. Until then, design as if it flows — don't strip the case.

items.summary: TakeAction + EndTurn handlers check enc.Mode() first; return FailedPrecondition if not TURN_BASED
After EndTurn advances initiative, handler inspects new active actor; if NPC, calls enc.NPCAct and recursively cycles through any subsequent NPC turns
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.8 (rpg-api PR #507). The EndTurn handler doesn't just advance initiative — it drives the NPC cycle until the next player is active:

  enc.EndTurn(viewer)  // advances ActiveIdx, may wrap round
  for i := 0; i < len(enc.InitiativeOrder()) + 4; i++ {
      active := enc.ActiveActor()
      if active is a player → break
      if active is an NPC → enc.NPCAct(active)  // toolkit publishes the NPC's turn events
      // loop continues; NPCAct calls EndTurn internally, so the next iteration sees the new active actor
  }

Loop bound = initiative_size + 4 — defensive cap against an infinite cycle if every actor is somehow an NPC. Designed in the Wave 2.8 plan; verified at playtest as one client RPC producing 5 events in a single response: `EndTurn(bob) → TurnEnded(bob) → TurnStarted(goblin) → EntityDamaged(alice) → TurnEnded(goblin) → TurnStarted(alice round=2)`.

The NPC's turn events fire from inside the toolkit (via enc.NPCAct → monster.TakeTurn → bus → broker), so the handler does NOT manually publish them. The handler's only responsibility is the cycle. Keep the cap loose enough for many-NPC encounters but tight enough to fail loudly on a real bug.

Future: when reactions / opportunity attacks land, this loop becomes more involved (reactions interleave between turns). For now, simple cycle-until-player is sufficient.

items.summary: Combat events: DamageDealt → EntityDamaged; ConditionApplied → StatusApplied; mode/turn events → corresponding proto events; AttackResolved drops on the floor today (#635)
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.8 (rpg-api PR #507). The translator's TranslateEvent type-switch added cases for the Wave 2.8 toolkit events:

  - DamageDealtEvent → encounterv2pb.EntityDamaged (target id, amount, hp_after.current/max)
  - ConditionAppliedEvent → encounterv2pb.StatusApplied (target id, condition ref, source ref, duration)
  - ModeChangedEvent → encounterv2pb.ModeChanged (new mode)
  - TurnStartedEvent → encounterv2pb.TurnStarted (active entity id, round)
  - TurnEndedEvent → encounterv2pb.TurnEnded (entity id that just ended)
  - AttackResolvedEvent → encounterv2pb.AttackResolved (cause-stage; not currently on wire — see below)

All cases honor pat-v2-translator-typed-errors: ErrViewerSawNothing for empty per-viewer slices, ErrUnknownEventType for unrecognized types.

Validated reality note (2026-05-09): AttackResolvedEvent does NOT fire on the wire today. The dnd5e action layer (bite, scimitar, melee, ranged) only publishes the cause AttackEvent without resolution data; the encounter SDK uses a stand-in resolver to compute hit/damage from monster snapshot fields instead of routing through combat.ResolveAttack. Tracked as rpg-toolkit#635. The translator's AttackResolved case is wired and tested — it just doesn't get exercised yet. Once #635 lands, AttackResolved will start flowing and animation-layer consumers can subscribe to it.

When adding new combat event types: extend TranslateEvent + add a translateCombatXxx helper that handles per-viewer slicing + add a translate_combat_test.go case. Keep cause and effect as separate cases — see pat-v2-cause-effect-event-split.

items.summary: Every wave that adds fields to encounter.Data MUST update ProjectFor in the same PR; live events and snapshot projection are TWO paths
items.details:
Discovered during Wave 2.8 playtest 2026-05-09. The combat handlers in PR #506/#507 wired LIVE event flow correctly — taking actions and rolling initiative produced the right wire events. But the SNAPSHOT path on initial connect / reconnect / refresh sent an Encounter proto missing the Wave 2.8 fields:

  - data.Mode → projection hardcoded ENCOUNTER_MODE_FREE_ROAM
  - data.Initiative + ActiveIdx + Round → no TurnState built
  - data.Monsters → only player entities iterated
  - PlayerData → entities lacked type + HP + CharacterData oneof

Result: clients that joined late or refreshed mid-combat saw mode=UNSPECIFIED. The web combat panel gates on `mode === 'TURN_BASED'`, so the harness combat section never enabled — even though the live events were correct. Fixed across rpg-api#509 (mode + turn_state + monsters), #510 (player type/HP/CharacterData), #511/#512 (player projection).

The lesson: ProjectFor in `internal/handlers/dnd5e/v2/encounter/project.go` is the second path that consumes encounter.Data. Live event handlers update Data + emit events; snapshot projection reads Data and emits a single Encounter proto. Forgetting to update ProjectFor surfaces only when a viewer connects fresh — silent for the lifetime of any session that started from an empty encounter.

Wave checklist whenever encounter.Data grows new fields:
  1. Toolkit publishes new events → translator gets new cases (pat-v2-combat-event-translator).
  2. Toolkit aggregate persists new state on Data → ProjectFor MUST consume that state and emit it on the wire shape.
  3. Both paths covered by test fixtures: handler suite for live events, project_test.go for snapshot.
  4. Manual seed-and-refresh playtest confirms a fresh client sees the same world a live client sees.

If a wave plan describes both new events AND new Data fields, the close-the-loop reviewer should sanity-check both halves landed. Reference: rpg-api#509 issue body for the proof and fix sketch.

items.summary: Caller-private prompts ride on InteractResponse.input_required / TakeActionResponse.input_required, never as a stream event
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.9 (rpg-api PR #515). Prompts (skill check / dialogue / target select) are caller-private game state — only the player who triggered the prompt should see the DC, ability, and tool requirements. They flow on the unary RPC response (`InteractResponse.input_required` field 2; `TakeActionResponse.input_required` field 2), NOT through the encounter Broker.

The contract has carried `InputRequired` / `SkillCheckPrompt` since Phase 1 (`types.proto:284-317`); Wave 2.9 was the first verb to populate it. The Interact handler, after detecting a locked-door target, builds an `InputRequired{skill_check: {dc, ability, tool}}` and sets it on the InteractResponse — and emits zero stream events for the prompt itself. The world-affecting outcome (door opens or stays closed) flows through the Broker once SubmitCheck resolves the prompt.

Why never on the stream:
  - Other viewers should NOT learn the DC / ability / tool of another player's pending check (info leak about narrative state).
  - The Broker fan-out delivers to all subscribers; per-viewer slicing exists for outcome events but is the wrong shape for a single-recipient prompt.
  - The caller already has the response in hand to drive UI; no second round-trip needed.

When adding a future prompt-issuing RPC (e.g., `BeginDialogue`): set `input_required` on its response, do NOT publish a `PromptIssued` event. The outcome of the prompt's resolution flows on the stream as normal world events.

items.summary: SubmitCheck handler delegates entirely to the toolkit Encounter aggregate; no rules logic in rpg-api
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.9 (rpg-api PR #515). `internal/handlers/dnd5e/v2/encounter/submit_check.go` is a thin shim over `enc.SubmitCheck(playerID, roll)`. The handler:

  1. Auth → `auth.GetPlayerID(ctx)`; empty → Unauthenticated.
  2. Validate request shape: empty `EncounterId` / `EntityId` → InvalidArgument; roll outside [1,20] → InvalidArgument.
  3. Load encounter via `encRepo.Get` + `encounter.LoadFromData(data, broker, encounter.WithCharacterResolver(h.resolver))`.
  4. Call `enc.SubmitCheck(playerID, roll)` — toolkit verb owns: pending-prompt lookup, ability-modifier math, tool-proficiency bonus, total computation, success comparison, dispatch to `triggeredAction` (e.g. `OpenDoor`), pending-prompt clearing.
  5. Map toolkit errors via pat-v2-status-code-mapping: `ErrNoPendingPrompt` → FailedPrecondition; missing target → NotFound; etc.
  6. Save encounter via `encRepo.Save(enc.ToData())`.
  7. Return `SubmitCheckResponse{success, total}`.

Events (DoorOpened + HexRevealed on success) fire from inside the toolkit during `enc.SubmitCheck`; the handler does NOT manually publish them. Same convention as the other v2 verbs (pat-v2-handler-direct-no-orchestrator, pat-v2-interact-handler-shape).

When extending SubmitCheck to new prompt kinds (DialogueChoice, TargetSelect): add the dispatch case inside the toolkit's `dispatchPromptAction`, not the handler. The handler stays thin — only auth, validate, load, call, save, map errors, return.

items.summary: Interact (and any future prompt-issuing RPC) returns FailedPrecondition if the caller already has a pending prompt; server enforces 'at most one pending'
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.9 (rpg-api PR #515). The pending-prompt invariant from `design.md §4` ("a player can have at most one pending prompt at a time") is enforced server-side. When the caller invokes Interact while `encounter.Data.PendingPrompts[playerID]` is non-nil, the toolkit returns `ErrPromptAlreadyPending` and the handler maps it to `codes.FailedPrecondition` ("resolve pending prompt first"). Per feedback_no_logic_in_web, the web does NOT gate on pending-prompt state — it just calls the RPC and surfaces the error.

This collision rule applies to:
  - Interact on a locked door while another check is pending (e.g., player triggered a dialogue prompt from an NPC and now tries to pick a lock without resolving).
  - Future prompt-issuing RPCs (BeginDialogue, etc.) follow the same rule.

MoveEntity, EndTurn, TakeAction (non-prompt-issuing actions) are NOT gated by pending-prompt state in Wave 2.9 — their semantics don't conflict with an outstanding skill check. If a future wave decides movement should pause during prompts, that's an explicit gate addition, not a default.

Resolution path: caller submits SubmitCheck (success OR failure clears the prompt — see pat-v2-thread-resolver-everywhere reality note in toolkit-member's pat-encounter-pending-prompt) and may then re-issue Interact.

When wiring a new prompt-issuing RPC: copy the pre-flight check from interact.go's locked-door branch — load encounter, check `data.PendingPrompts[playerID]`, return FailedPrecondition early if non-nil. Don't try to enqueue / queue prompts; the design choice is single-slot, fail-fast.

items.summary: WithCharacterResolver(h.resolver) MUST thread through every LoadFromData / tkenc.New call site so SubmitCheck can run modifier math regardless of which prior verb created the encounter state
items.details:
Discovered during Wave 2.9 implementation (rpg-api#515). The toolkit's `SubmitCheck` verb computes `roll + ability_modifier(playerID, prompt.ability) + tool_proficiency_bonus(playerID, prompt.tool)` — both lookups go through the `CharacterResolver` interface that `encounter.WithCharacterResolver(...)` wires in at LoadFromData / tkenc.New time. If any prior verb in the encounter's lifetime called `encounter.LoadFromData(data, broker)` WITHOUT the resolver option, the encounter's runtime aggregate has no resolver attached. SubmitCheck against that encounter then returns `ErrNoCharacterResolver` even though the resolver is sitting on the handler struct.

The fix: every handler that constructs or rehydrates an encounter must thread `encounter.WithCharacterResolver(h.resolver)`:

  - CreateEncounter (`tkenc.New(id, broker, encounter.WithCharacterResolver(h.resolver))`)
  - MoveEntity
  - EndTurn
  - TakeAction
  - Interact
  - SubmitCheck

`ProjectFor` (read-only — calls `LoadFromData` then `SnapshotFor`) is the one exception that's safe to skip: it never calls a verb that needs modifier math. But threading the option there too is harmless and keeps the call-site shape uniform.

Failure mode is silent until SubmitCheck runs against an encounter created by a non-resolver-wired path — e.g., player creates an encounter, walks around, opens the locked door's prompt, submits a roll → `ErrNoCharacterResolver`. The other verbs work fine without the resolver because they don't touch character state.

Reference rpg-api#515 for the discovery story. When adding a new v2 verb that constructs/rehydrates an encounter: include `encounter.WithCharacterResolver(h.resolver)` in the option list at the call site, even if the verb itself doesn't need it. Future verbs that DO need it will inherit the wired runtime.

items.summary: Encounter end is server-side terminal state (toolkit Mode == ModeEnded); verbs check terminal state first and return FailedPrecondition with ErrEncounterEnded
Death is two events: EntityDied (cause/narrative) + EntityRemoved (effect/state mutation); same shape as AttackResolved + DamageDealt from Wave 2.8
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.10 (rpg-api PR #517 + rpg-toolkit PR #643). Entity death surfaces on the wire as TWO distinct events:

  - EntityDiedEvent — CAUSE / narrative. Carries the dying entity id, killer attribution (PlayerID or NPC EntityID), and any narrative payload (kill type, dramatic flag). Consumers: log lines ("alice slays the goblin"), animations (death throes), kill-attribution overlays.
  - EntityRemovedEvent — EFFECT / state mutation. Carries only the removed entity id. Consumers: entity-table reducer drops the entry; spatial layer prunes from collision; turn-order display splices.

Wave 2.10 fires them BACK-TO-BACK from inside the toolkit's `killEntity` helper (see toolkit pat-encounter-death-detection): EntityDied → delete from data → splice initiative → EntityRemoved → checkEncounterEnd. But future waves may DELAY EntityRemoved for corpse mechanics (loot, resurrection windows, body-as-cover). Web handles them independently — the cause-effect split holds regardless of timing.

Same shape as Wave 2.8's AttackResolved (cause) + DamageDealt (effect) split from pat-v2-cause-effect-event-split. The translator MUST NOT collapse the two; one toolkit event → one wire event, always.

Viewer slicing: EntityDied is per-viewer (LoS gates whether you see the kill); EntityRemoved is broadcast — see pat-v2-translator-broadcast-event for the projection asymmetry. A viewer might see EntityRemoved without EntityDied if they had LoS on the position but not on the killer.

When adding new lifecycle events (Resurrected, Banished, Polymorphed): same cause-effect split. Narrative cause + state-mutation effect, separate per-viewer projection rules. Cross-link with toolkit pat-encounter-death-detection.

items.summary: Some translated events (EntityRemoved, EncounterEnded) are global state mutations that bypass per-viewer projection — always broadcast to all encounter participants
items.details:
Shipped in Wave 2.10 (rpg-api PR #517). The translator's per-viewer projection rule (each viewer's `PerPlayer[viewer]` slice gates what they see) has an explicit BROADCAST exception for events that represent global state mutations the entire encounter must converge on:

  - EntityRemovedEvent — every viewer must drop the entity from their local model. Hiding removal from a viewer would leave a ghost in their UI that no longer exists server-side.
  - EncounterEndedEvent — every viewer must transition to terminal-state UI. Hiding end from a viewer would let them keep clicking buttons on a stopped encounter.

Distinct from per-viewer events (EntityDamaged, MoveEvent, EntityDied) which derive audience from LoS / PerceptionView. The translator's per-viewer code path either:
  (a) skips projection entirely for broadcast events (no `ErrViewerSawNothing` possible), OR
  (b) builds a synthetic per-viewer slice that always returns visible=true for every viewer.

The translate.go test suite must cover broadcast events with a multi-viewer fixture and assert all viewers receive the wire event regardless of LoS state.

Decision rule for new events: if the event represents authoritative WORLD STATE that all clients must see to stay consistent, broadcast. If the event represents a NARRATIVE OBSERVATION ("alice attacked the goblin"), per-viewer. EntityDied is narrative — alice's stealth attack on a hidden goblin shouldn't reveal to bob that the goblin existed and is now dead.

Reference rpg-api#517 and the cross-link to pat-v2-cause-effect-death-events (which describes the cause-effect pair where the effect happens to be broadcast).

items.summary: Toolkit core.ModeEnded maps to wire ENCOUNTER_MODE_FREE_ROAM (no _ENDED enum value in v1alpha2); the dedicated EncounterEndedEvent is the canonical wire signal for end
items.details:
Discovered during Wave 2.10 implementation (rpg-api PR #517). The toolkit's `core.ModeEnded` is a third mode value alongside `FreeRoam` and `TurnBased`, but the v1alpha2 `EncounterMode` enum does NOT have a corresponding `ENCOUNTER_MODE_ENDED` value. Adding one would have been a breaking change to the proto contract late in the wave; the design choice instead is:

  - Wire mode field: when `enc.Mode() == core.ModeEnded`, project as `ENCOUNTER_MODE_FREE_ROAM` (the original pre-combat mode value).
  - Canonical end signal: the dedicated `EncounterEndedEvent` is what clients consume to detect end. Snapshot replay for late-joiners includes terminal projection (entity table empty of monsters, no active actor, etc.) but the mode field reads as FREE_ROAM.

Don't try to surface ModeEnded as a wire mode value — clients should subscribe to EncounterEnded for end detection, not poll the mode field. The web reducer mirror is `encounterStatus: 'active' | 'ended'` derived from EncounterEnded handler (see web-side pat-v2-encounter-status-reducer).

Future proto evolution: when v1beta cuts, ENCOUNTER_MODE_ENDED MAY be added — at which point the projection logic would map directly. Until then, the dual-channel signal (mode=FREE_ROAM + EncounterEndedEvent) is the contract.

A known consequence: the harness's mode header indicator stays as FREE_ROAM after end (filed as rpg-dnd5e-web#406; see web pat-v2-stale-display-on-removal). That display drift is web-only — server enforcement is correct because verbs gate on `enc.Mode() == ModeEnded`, not on the wire mode field.

Reference rpg-api#518 + rpg-api PR #517's design choice.

items.summary: EndTurn handler's NPC dispatch loop checks enc.Mode() == ModeEnded after each NPCAct/EndTurn cycle and breaks; cheap forward-loading insurance for future faction/NPC-on-NPC kills
Wall consumers load the union of all revealed rooms' walls in dungeon-absolute, not just currentRoom.Walls
items.details:
Issue #465 (wall-consumer scope, separate from the type-unification scope tracked under the same issue number). Before this rule, every wall-aware path in the encounter orchestrator wrote a snippet like:

  if currentRoom := dungeon.GetRoom(currentRoomID); currentRoom != nil {
      dungeonWalls = currentRoom.Walls
  }

That is wrong any time more than one room is revealed. Once the player walks through OpenDoor, every other revealed room's perimeter is invisible to collision and to the wall set published in events.

The rule: use loadAbsoluteWallsForRevealedRooms(dng) in revealed_walls.go. It iterates dng.RevealedRooms, applies each room's origin (from dng.RoomOrigins) to every wall vertex element-wise, and returns the union in dungeon-absolute. The validator PathCrossesWall (and wallsToBlockedHexes for monster perception) is a 2D-segment-intersection / cube-rasterization function — frame-agnostic, so absolute-on-absolute works.

Consumers that must use the union:
- MoveCharacter (orchestrator.go ~1620): wall-collision check.
- executeMoveAction (orchestrator.go ~5290): wall-collision per path step.
- executeMonsterTurns (monster_turns.go ~50): perception BlockedHexes + validateMovementAgainstWalls.
- ResolveAttack (orchestrator.go ~520): AttackResolved event Walls field.
- EndTurn (orchestrator.go ~2065): TurnEnded / MonsterTurnCompleted event Walls field.

Door positions are passable by construction — perimeter generation (internal/components/dungeon/toolkit/perimeter.go) splits walls AROUND the door hex via createWallBeforeDoor / createWallAfterDoor, so the door is a gap in the wall list. No special-case logic needed in the collision check.

If you write a new consumer that calls dungeon.GetRoom(currentRoomID).Walls and treats that as the encounter wall set, you reproduce #465. Enforce this at code review.
